_comment: TEMPLATE -- roster overrides for the 2027 season projection. Fill in the
'assignments' list below. As shipped it is EMPTY, which changes nothing:
every player keeps the team inferred from his most recent playing time.
Why fill it in: that inference is wrong for every offseason move until the
season's data exists. List each signing, trade, retirement and correction
here and re-run (see README: a full run_pipeline.py run applies team changes
to the club playing-time closure, then season_engine.py and the export).
A move recomputes BOTH clubs' run environments, so both lineups' R/RBI shift.
Each assignment (add one object per player to the list):
player_id  (required) MLBAM id -- the PlayerId column in out/*.csv.
Find it with e.g.:  grep -i 'judge' out/hitter_pa_projections_2027.csv
team       club code or full name: ARI ATL BAL BOS CHC CIN CLE COL CWS DET
HOU KC LAA LAD MIA MIL MIN NYM NYY OAK/ATH PHI PIT SD SEA SF STL
TB TEX TOR WSH (also 'CHW', 'New York Yankees', ...).
Special values:
"FA"  unsigned free agent: keeps his full rate line and gets
playing time from his role, but sits outside all 30 clubs.
Assign him a club here once he signs.
null  team genuinely unknown (bad id/data). NOT the same as FA.
team_id    alternative to 'team': explicit MLBAM team id (e.g. 147 = NYY).
note       free text, ignored by the loader. Record the move and its date.
Example entries (copy into 'assignments', then edit):
{"player_id": 592450, "team": "SF",  "note": "signed 2026-12-01"}
{"player_id": 660271, "team_id": 147, "note": "traded 2026-12-10"}
{"player_id": 111111, "team": "FA",  "note": "unsigned, 2026-12-01"}
(Those ids/moves are illustrative only -- do not paste them in as real.)
Unresolvable teams and entries with no usable player_id are skipped with a
warning, not a failure. Ids that match nobody are silently harmless, so
double-check an id if a move seems to have no effect.
See rosters/team_assignments.example.json for the long-form explanation and
the 'reserves' block (leave it empty; it does nothing in the default mode).
